$comment: SSOT for scripts/render-distributions.mjs. Paths were probed 2026-08-09; `consumes` entries must exist in this repo and `output.repo` must be a real remote, both enforced by validate:agent-plugins. The renderer landed 2026-08-13 (Tier 2.1) and reads `renderKind` + `renders`: `renderKind` states how a target relates to this repo and an unrecognized value is an error, so a new target cannot be added without deciding — a target with no declared kind would otherwise be skipped in silence. Only `projection` targets emit files, and validate:render-drift byte-compares every one of them against its canonical source.

canonicalTree.$comment: `skills` is GENERATED by skills-sync (`npm run skills:export`), gitignored, and never committed (decided 2026-08-12). The distribution renderer must PRODUCE this directory, not drift-check a tracked one; there is no committed baseline to compare against and there deliberately is not going to be. The `agent-plugins` registration in server/skills-sync.yaml ships empty, because an entry there would make this repo's guess the default for every installation — see server/skills-sync.example.yaml for the enable path. `manifest` and `mcp` ARE committed and ARE drift-checkable.

targets.notes: Published as a release asset (Tier 4.1), not a repo render. `renders` is empty because this target's source and output are the same files — the canonical tree is what ships. Staging is `extension-publish.yml`'s plugin-dist job.

targets.namespaceStatus: n/a — Anthropic is not on the standard; this is a permanent legacy render
targets.notes: The only target with a real file-copy relationship, and therefore the whole subject of the drift gate. `consumes` lists what the PUBLISHING jobs stage; `renders` lists what this repo generates from the canonical pair — the two overlap on the manifests and are not the same list. Both extension-publish.yml jobs that stage these files now run the drift check before staging. marketplace.json pins sourceRef 'dist'.

targets.namespaceStatus: unresolved — Gemini CLI is not an Agent Plugins launch client; extension format is its own
targets.notes: MEASURED 2026-08-13, correcting this entry: gemini-prompts is NOT a file render of this repo. It consumes the server and hook library as the npm package `claude-prompts` — `gemini-prompts/hooks/lib` is a symlink into `node_modules/claude-prompts/hooks/lib`, and its own `hooks/hooks.json` + `hooks/gate-enforce.py` DIFFER from ours because Gemini CLI's events differ (BeforeAgent/BeforeTool vs UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse). The previous `consumes: [hooks, server/dist]` and `hookMapping` described a copy that does not exist; validate:agent-plugins passed it because it only asked whether those paths exist HERE, never whether the target consumes them that way. Per-release update is the dependency-range bump in extension-publish.yml's sync-downstream job. Contract: .claude/rules/extension-alignment.md. Tier 2b listing URLs pin this repo, so the URL must not change.

targets.namespaceStatus: unresolved — OpenCode is not an Agent Plugins launch client; plugin format is its own
targets.notes: MEASURED 2026-08-13, correcting this entry: opencode-prompts tracks no `hooks/` and no `server/` — it is an independent TypeScript port (`src/`, `index.ts`), so there is nothing here to render into it. `consumes: [server/dist]` asserted a copy that never existed. Its `buildStep` is its OWN build of its OWN source, not a step this renderer runs; it stays recorded because Tier 5.2 needs it. Per-release update is the dependency-range bump in extension-publish.yml's sync-downstream job. Contract: .claude/rules/extension-alignment.md — "a behavioral port, not an adapter port; nothing is shared with the TS rewrite".

unresolved.clientNamespaces: Agent Plugins 1.0.0 puts hooks in reverse-domain namespace dirs (com.example.client/), but v1 defines NO core hooks. The concrete namespace string for each launch client (Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Kiro, VS Code) is not published in the spec text and is NOT guessed here. Resolving it is a prerequisite for Tier 4.1 — see the plan's risk row 'Codex namespace unknown'.
